answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may place orders, with bond size rising as it opens more accounts. A wharf operator can mirror-check withdrawals against the bonded ledger and slash the stake when linked accounts evade limits or default. Sybils then cannot gain influence merely by multiplying names: each name ties up real capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing it. The timber market may still admit wealthy attackers, so the bond raises the cost rather than proving identity.
